amendments.primary_scoring_effect: NONE. Mean party-level fair CRPS, its availability condition, the final date, and the winner rule are unchanged.

Fallback-B WIS values are rescaled to the standard definition. This cannot change the ElectionSimulator-versus-Botten-Ada ranking or winner because both are scored on the same common interval levels and therefore share the same positive denominator. Draw-based primary fair CRPS is unchanged.

A deterministically reproduced ElectionSimulator draw sidecar may qualify as REPLAY_VERIFIED and therefore may satisfy ElectionSimulator's draw-availability side of fallback level A. This can change which pre-registered scoring tier is available, but does not change fair CRPS, the requirement that both systems have verified predictive draws, the final date, party set, or winner rule.

Retaining a same-SimulationResult sidecar for every certified production generation can change which draws exist and therefore which pre-registered fallback tier is available. It does not change any scoring rule: fair CRPS and the standard WIS of amendment 002 are unchanged, as are the requirement that both systems have verified predictive draws, the cutoff rules, the party set, the final forecast date, and the winner hierarchy.

NONE. The cutoff, the timing-eligibility rule, the late-capture limit, the fair CRPS primary metric and its availability condition, the party set, the final forecast date and the winner hierarchy are all unchanged. Only the wall-clock time at which the scheduled job begins its preparation changes.

NONE. The cutoff, the timing-eligibility rule, the late-capture limit, the capture dates, the fair CRPS primary metric and its availability condition, the amendment 002 standard WIS formula, the amendment 003 and 004 exact-draw rules, the eight-party set, the final forecast date and the winner hierarchy are all unchanged. Only the mechanism by which the scheduled trigger is delivered changes.
